criteria_source: The fixture only. schema.sql stores every monetary column - plans.monthly_price, ledger_entries.amount, invoices.total - as DOUBLE PRECISION, and the trailing comment defines an account balance as sum(amount) over ledger_entries. IEEE 754 binary floating point cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly, so summing a ledger in it accumulates error; PostgreSQL 16 offers NUMERIC for this. The fact is about the database, not about rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the answer names the DOUBLE PRECISION money columns as the defect to fix before a ledger is built on them - binary floating point cannot represent decimal amounts exactly, so a summed balance drifts - and points at NUMERIC/DECIMAL or integer minor units. Naming any one of the three money columns is enough. The money type must be given as the defect that decides the answer: the reason this schema does not hold up under the ledger the trailing comment describes, whose balance is defined as sum(amount) over ledger_entries. Fails when the answer calls the schema sound, or raises only the missing currency consistency constraint, indexing, the nullable canceled_at, the CHECK lists, normalization, or a missing updated_at while leaving the float money type unchallenged. Also fails when the money type is named but presented as one member of a set of defects offered as equally decisive - no append-only guarantee, no idempotency key, no sign convention tied to entry_type, no per-currency grouping. Those are real gaps and naming them is not itself a failure, but none of them touches the arithmetic the ledger's balance is defined as, so an answer that weighs them alike has not told the user which change the ledger work depends on.
